links.comparator_used: fully automated model classifying every slide (and fully manual IHC plus pathologist review of all slides)
links.outcome: diagnostic accuracy and IHC workload in lineage prediction with confidence-threshold deferral to IHC and manual review
links.effect: Fully automated model had 16.1% lower accuracy and 0.040 lower AUC than IHC/manual review in the prospective cohort (p<0.001). Semi-automated with threshold deferral gave 95.9% accuracy, comparable to full IHC/manual (p=0.610), with a 68.9% reduction in IHC workload. Internal test: threshold >0.8 gave accuracy comparable to manual (p=0.856), with 78.0% auto-subtyped. External cohort: cutoff 0.8 gave 86.0% accuracy; cutoff 0.9 gave 95.1% accuracy (p=0.293 vs manual) with 39.3% workload reduction. Functional cohort: 99.0% accuracy, 74.4% workload reduction.
links.tradeoff: Raising the cutoff improves accuracy but reduces workload savings (external cohort: 86.0% accuracy at 0.8 vs 95.1% accuracy with only 39.3% reduction at 0.9). Low-confidence cases still need IHC staining and manual review. Determinants of the confidence index are not fully characterized.
links.quote: In the prospective cohort, the implementation of the semi-automated approach resulted in a 68.9% reduction in the workload of IHC staining.

links.comparator_used: a lower confidence cutoff of 0.8 versus a higher cutoff of 0.9 in the external cohort (different centers)
links.outcome: accuracy of semi-automated lineage prediction in the external cohort with a raised confidence cutoff
links.effect: External cohort: cutoff 0.8 yielded 86.0% accuracy; raising to 0.9 improved accuracy to 95.1%, statistically comparable to full IHC/manual evaluation (p=0.293), with workload reduction of 39.3%.
links.tradeoff: Higher cutoff reduces workload savings to 39.3%.
links.quote: Under this scenario, although the workload reduction was only 39.3%, the accuracy significantly improved to 95.1%.

links.comparator_used: uniform IHC staining and manual review of all slides
links.outcome: diagnostic workload and accuracy when only low-confidence cases are routed to IHC and pathologist review
links.effect: 68.9% reduction in IHC workload with 95.9% accuracy in the prospective cohort (p=0.610 vs full IHC/manual). Functional cohort 74.4% reduction and 99.0% accuracy. External cohort 39.3% reduction and 95.1% accuracy at cutoff 0.9.
links.tradeoff: Savings shrink as the cutoff is raised to maintain accuracy; escalated cases still require IHC staining (about 1,000 CNY per three-antibody panel) and manual review.
links.quote: The pipeline employs a dynamic confidence threshold: samples below this threshold undergo confirmatory IHC staining and manual pathological review, while those surpassing it are classified automatically.

design_hint: confidence threshold triage with confirmatory IHC and manual pathology review
